_meta.indication: COMETRIQ is indicated for the treatment of patients with progressive, metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC).

pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal (registration) trial; FDA agreed on study design via EOP2/preNDA meeting and SPA
pivotal_trials.design: Single international, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with actively progressing, measurable or non-measurable metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) as determined by an independent central review committee (IRC) masked to treatment assignment
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant PFS improvement: median 11.2 months (cabozantinib) vs 4.0 months (placebo); Hazard Ratio 0.28 (95% CI 0.19, 0.40); p<0.0001. Overall response rate 27% vs 0; p<0.0001. No OS benefit demonstrated at the interim OS analysis (interim OS HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.64, 1.54); the protocol-specified final OS analysis remained to be submitted.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥25%): diarrhea (63% vs 33% placebo), stomatitis (51% vs 6%), PPES (50% vs 2%), decreased weight (48% vs 10%), decreased appetite (46% vs 18%), nausea (43% vs 21%), fatigue (41% vs 28%). Serious/boxed risks include GI perforations (3%) and severe/fatal hemorrhage (3%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 6% of COMETRIQ patients.
target_moa: Cabozantinib is a small molecule inhibitor of multiple receptor-based tyrosine kinases, including RET, MET, and VEGFR2 (as well as VEGFR1, VEGFR3, FLT3, TIE2, Axl, TrkB and KIT), developed as a targeted therapy based on the correlation between RET gene mutation and MTC.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: PERFORATIONS AND FISTULAS, and HEMORRHAGE — GI perforations occurred in 3% and fistula formation in 1% of COMETRIQ-treated patients (discontinue for perforation/fistula); severe, sometimes fatal hemorrhage including hemoptysis and GI hemorrhage occurred in 3% of COMETRIQ-treated patients.

rems.type: The applicant did not propose a REMS and the review team did not identify the need for a REMS to ensure safe use of cabozantinib.

companion_dx_detail: RET mutation assessment was not required by the protocol; it was assessed retrospectively in approximately 70% of patients with research-use-only assays and no companion diagnostic was required.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical study design was acceptable and the application raised no significant safety/efficacy issues or controversial issues.

basis.text: The application was designated Priority review.

summary.text: COMETRIQ (cabozantinib) received Fast-track designation (April 8, 2011) and Orphan drug designation (November 29, 2010) for medullary thyroid carcinoma, and the NDA was reviewed under Priority review. It was a first-cycle, full (not accelerated) approval based on the single randomized placebo-controlled trial XL184-301.
